scenes.title: Geometric Meaning of Eigenvalues
scenes.description: Focus on the Eigenvectors to show the scaling effect. Positive λ stretches, negative λ flips and stretches, |λ| > 1 or < 1 determines magnitude.

scenes.title: Diagonalization as a Change of Basis
scenes.description: Visualize aligning the coordinate axes with the Eigenvectors. Show that in this new basis, the transformation matrix becomes diagonal (D), representing pure scaling along axes.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Recap that diagonalization allows us to understand complex transformations by breaking them down into independent scalings along principal axes.

key_points: Eigenvectors represent directions that remain unchanged (except for scaling) during a transformation.
Eigenvalues represent the factor by which the Eigenvector is scaled.
Diagonalization is the process of finding a basis where the transformation acts purely by scaling.
educational.emphasis: Focus on the geometric intuition of 'staying on the same line' rather than the algebraic calculation of determinants.
